prize_parts.citation: for discoveries establishing the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my preferred configuration is unchanged: a single part, B041, crediting Daniel J. Drucker, Jens Juul Holst and Svetlana Mojsov. I do not rely on the six-way agreement; the exchange mainly tested the attribution and the alternatives, and B041 held up on the science. The arc runs from incretin physiology and the secretion and actions of GLP-1, through identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form, to a drug class with large, independent outcome evidence in diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular and renal disease. The mechanism is confirmed over decades and the clinical effect is at its peak, so the timing is right. Naming three steps (physiology and secretion, biology and translational actions, active-peptide identification) lets the citation describe what was discovered rather than which product succeeded. A single part is also the only structure that fits the chair's questions without damaging either achievement: a two-part prize would cut B041 to two names and leave at most one name for a second part, and no name in B041 can be removed without breaking the physiological story.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakness and the exchange did not remove it. Knudsen's long-acting analogue design is what made the drugs usable, and Wahren-Herlenius is right that calling it merely industrial understates it. The citation should therefore say plainly that it honours the physiology and the active form, and that the drug-design step is outside it, not that it is minor. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide against other early workers, including Habener, cannot be settled from the material I am permitted to read, and I am not willing to treat the contested point as resolved in either direction. If the committee decides that the achievement is the drug, my three names are incomplete and one of them would have to give way, and I have no documented ground for choosing which. The strongest fallback is B030 narrowed to June and Sadelain, which is equally mature but carries the unresolved credit of the chimeric receptor originators such as Eshhar.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius says that calling Knudsen's work merely translational understates it, since the drugs that changed care are her designs and the prize has honoured therapeutic development before, and that the committee should admit the choice leaves a real gap.
responses.response: I agree with the framing and have adjusted my wording. In round 1 I said her work should not be dismissed as industrial, and I now go further: the citation and the committee record should state that excluding Knudsen is a judgment about which discovery the prize names, not a finding about her contribution. Where I part from your fallback of a prize split between physiology and translation is arithmetic and coherence. Within three names, a translation part would force one of Drucker, Holst or Mojsov out of the physiology part, and I do not see documented grounds to say which one is least central. So I keep the physiology trio.

responses.point: Sandberg moved toward a two-person B030 for June and Sadelain, noted that Eshhar has a stronger claim to the receptor concept than Rosenberg, and argued that waiting on B041 would cost little if the credit dispute cannot be resolved because CAR-T is equally mature.
responses.response: I accept the attribution reasoning on B030 and agree the two-name form is more defensible than three, though Eshhar's absence remains a real gap. I do not accept the inference that B041 can wait. The credit uncertainty in B041 is a cut among four documented contributors, and it is bounded: the physiology trio can be argued from the record. The B030 uncertainty concerns who originated the concept, which is a harder and less bounded question. Delay also does not reduce either uncertainty, since neither can be resolved from the supplied files. For those reasons I keep B030 as my first alternative and not as the better prize.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks B023 (BCR-ABL inhibition) above B035, would keep any B035 citation strictly mechanistic, and says he would reopen Knudsen's place only if the citation were framed around the drugs.
responses.response: On B035 I agree on a strictly mechanistic citation for Mori and Walter, and I concede that the integrated stress response translation is still developing, so I would not argue it ahead of a clinically proven alternative. I keep it as my second alternative because it has the cleanest two-person allocation on the list, whereas B023 depends on prior chromosomal and kinase biology and industrial chemistry, as El-Manira argued. On Knudsen, your condition is the right one and I accept it: if the committee frames the citation around the drugs, the argument must be about which of the three is least central, and we should not assume it is Mojsov.

responses.point: El-Manira says that Ron's PERK and CHOP work leaves a visible gap in B035 and that its medical consequences are still developing, and he also cautions that near-unanimity may reflect the salience of the weight-loss drugs rather than careful credit analysis.
responses.response: Both points are fair. The PERK and CHOP gap is a real limit on B035 and is the main reason I place it behind B041 and B030 and treat it as a candidate for a later year. Your caution about salience is why I set out the credit analysis step by step: each of the three names is tied to a distinct discovery that had to exist before the drugs could be designed. I still cannot verify the priority questions around the active peptide, so the test I apply is whether the record supports each name for the step the citation assigns, not how prominent the drugs are.

responses.point: Linnarsson would not dismiss Rosenberg in B030, because his adoptive transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials set the clinical proof of concept, and he holds that Knudsen's role is a step further along the translational chain.
responses.response: On Rosenberg I accept that his early trials were important proof of concept, but they belong to the adoptive-transfer lineage and not the CAR itself. I would not add him to B030 at the cost of the two names with the CAR-specific contribution, and any three-name B030 would need a stated CAR-related ground for his inclusion, which I have not seen in the record. On Knudsen, I would put the step differently than you do: it is a different kind of discovery, not a lesser one, and saying so openly is what keeps the physiology citation honest.

uncertainties: Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide relative to Habener and other early workers; I cannot verify it from the permitted material and it is the main point that could change my allocation.
Whether the committee will define the B041 achievement as the physiology or as the drug, which would require Knudsen to displace one of the three without a documented basis for choosing whom.
Whether the originators of the chimeric receptor concept, such as Eshhar, and Rosenberg's role would alter a narrowed B030 if it were ever the fallback.
Whether the later translation of the integrated stress response would eventually strengthen B035 beyond a purely mechanistic case.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. My profile documents roughly twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann on dopamine neurons, Nurr1 and autophagy, and a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard. None of this relates to B041, B030 or B035 or their credited names, and the round-1 exchange raised no new tie. I see no ground for recusal and disclose the Perlmann co-authorship only for transparency.
